title: SYSK Selects: How Caving Works
summary: SYSK Selects rerun of the classic episode on caving. Hosts explain what a cave is (any opening from the surface into the earth, often part of a karst landscape), the four main ways caves form (carbonic acid dissolution of limestone, erosion/abrasion by water, extremophile bacteria producing sulfuric acid, sea caves, and lava tubes), stalactites vs. stalagmites and speleothems, cave temperature stability and cave cave-dwelling animal classes (troglobites, troglophiles, trogloxenes), cave art such as the Southeastern Ceremonial Complex drawings in Tennessee and Lascaux and Chauvet in France, and the thrill of caving. Much of the middle covers practical caving advice: light sources including carbide lamps, helmets certified by the UIAA, clothing (avoid cotton), group size, never caving alone, staying put if lost, leaving no waste, and cave diving dangers including 2012 deaths in Florida. The episode also covers show caves like Ruby Falls and Carlsbad Caverns, urban exploration, Bonne Terre Mine in Missouri, and a listener mail segment about pizza in Pakistan.

segments.title: Intro and rerun setup
segments.summary: Josh introduces this SYSK Selects pick on caving and banter about the hosts' names and a shirt joke. Chuck and Josh discuss an article on Southeastern ceremonial cave art.

segments.title: What a cave is and how caves form
segments.summary: The hosts define a cave as any opening from the surface into the earth, often part of a karst landscape with sinkholes and aquifers. They describe four main formation processes: carbonic acid dissolving limestone, erosion by water, sulfuric acid produced by extremophile bacteria, and sea caves and lava tubes.

segments.title: Stalactites and stalagmites
segments.summary: Stalactites hang from the ceiling and stalagmites rise from the floor. Both are speleothems formed by calcite deposited from dripping water, growing about a quarter to an inch per century. Hosts describe formations nicknamed fried eggs and bacon.

segments.title: Cave animals and cave temperature
segments.summary: Hosts describe troglobites, troglophiles and trogloxenes, the blind cave animals, and the stable temperature inside caves, noting that the temperature varies with depth and that some caves show seasonal changes.

segments.title: Cave art and archaeology
segments.summary: Caves preserve artifacts and ancient art well because conditions are stable. Hosts discuss the French cave art at Lascaux (found in 1940) and Chauvet, and the bison drawings that appear to move in torchlight, along with the Herzog film Cave of Forgotten Dreams.

segments.title: Why people go caving and conservation ethics
segments.summary: Hosts discuss the thrill of discovery, the role of conservation among serious cavers, search and rescue volunteers, and the difference between caving and urban exploration rules about not breaking in or taking anything.

segments.title: Show caves and getting started
segments.summary: Hosts compare guided show caves such as Ruby Falls and Carlsbad Caverns with more challenging caving, and mention a concert held in a Tennessee cave. Kids can visit guided caves safely.

segments.title: Cave diving and flooded mines
segments.summary: Cave diving is described as extremely dangerous, with reference to seven deaths in 2012 including three in three days in Florida. Hosts describe Bonne Terre Mine in Missouri, a flooded former lead mine open for guided scuba diving.

segments.title: Gear, clothing and light sources
segments.summary: Hosts advise carrying at least three light sources and spare batteries, certified helmets, synthetic clothing rather than cotton, knee and elbow pads, and food and water. They describe the carbide lamp used by an experienced caver.

segments.title: Caving safety rules
segments.summary: Hosts cover group size of four to six, placing the slowest person in front, never caving alone, staying put when lost, carrying out waste, leaving a map and route with someone above ground, and procedures for injured cavers. Hosts also mention hypothermia, flooding and falls.

segments.title: Lovecraft tangent and closing caving notes
segments.summary: Hosts digress into H.P. Lovecraft stories and a physics paper on quantum explanations for Call of Cthulhu, then recommend searching the HowStuffWorks site for spelunking and mention base jumping into caves like Sótano de las Golondrinas.

segments.title: Listener mail: pizza in Pakistan
segments.summary: A listener named Nabiha describes pizza in Pakistan, including chicken toppings, no ham, beef seekh kebab stuffed crust at Pizza Hut, and local chains.

segments.title: Outro
segments.summary: Hosts invite listeners to contact the show on Twitter, Facebook, and email, and close the episode.
